A: قرأتَ القرآنَ دُخولَكَ الجنَّةَ
B: قرأتَ القرآنَ لِدُخولِكَ الجنَّةَ

A: أذهبُ إلى زيدٍ طلبَه إيّايَ
B: أذهبُ إلى زيدٍ لطلبِه إيّايَ

mafool-lahu-fihi-03.png.sentence:
A: خشيةَ اللهِ صلُّوا صلواتِكُم
B: بِخشيةِ اللهِ صلُّوا صلواتِكُم

mafool-lahu-fihi-04.png.sentence:
A: لِلإِلتقاءِ غدًا تكلَّمتُ بزيدٍ
B: الالتقاءَ غدًا تكلَّمتُ بزيدٍ

mafool-lahu-fihi-05.png.sentence:
A: تدرسُ فاطمةُ التجويدَ أن تقرأَ القرآنَ
B: تدرسُ فاطمةُ التجويدَ (لِ) أن تقرأَ القرآنَ

mafool-lahu-fihi-06.png.sentence:
A: صفحَ زيدٌ عن السفيهِ حِلمًا
B: صفحَ زيدٌ عن السفيهِ لِحِلمٍ

mafool-lahu-fihi-07.png.sentence:
A: صامَ زيدٌ ابتغاءً رضَا اللهِ
B: صامَ زيدٌ مبتغيًا رضَا الله

mafool-lahu-fihi-08.png.sentence:
A: ابتعدتُ عن الأسد لخوفٍ
B: ابتعدتُ عن الأسد خوفاً

mafool-lahu-fihi-09.png.sentence:
A: عاقب الوالدُ وَلَدَه (لِ) أن يُؤَدِّبَه
B: عاقب الوالدُ وَلَدَه أن يُؤَدِّبَه

mafool-lahu-fihi-10.png.sentence:
A: لا تدخل في المكان المتداعِي ضعفَه
B: لا تدخل في المكان المتداعِي لِضعفِه

mafool-lahu-fihi-11.png.sentence: أعطيتُ الفقيرَ خبزاً مَنْحةً صباحًا شفقةً

mafool-lahu-fihi-12.png.sentence: مَا بِكَ وزيدًا أمسِ فوقَ المسجدِ

mafool-lahu-fihi-13.png.sentence: احترامًا قُمتَ وكِتابَكَ أمامَ الأستاذِ نَشاطًا

mafool-lahu-fihi-14.png.sentence: إبراهيمُ كسرَ الأصنامَ فأسًا يومَ عيدِهم كَرْهًا للشرك

mafool-lahu-fihi-15.png.sentence: أَطِعِ اللَّه تشريفًا له وَدينَه كلَّ الإطاعةِ أبَدًا

mafool-lahu-fihi-16.png.sentence: دخلتُ مكَّةَ للعمرة ارتجاءً مغفرةَ اللهِ

mafool-lahu-fihi-18.png.sentence: أَبْحَرَ زيدٌ السفينةَ ليلًا هُدُوءً له
mafool-lahu-fihi-18.png.doubt: At this image resolution a single fatha stroke and a doubled tanween-fatha stroke on the last letter of هُدُوءً are hard to tell apart with full certainty; same for the fatha mark over السفينةَ's final taa marbuta versus no mark there.

mafool-lahu-fihi-e05b.answer: Sentence B, تدرسُ فاطمةُ التجويدَ (لِ) أن تقرأَ القرآنَ, is correct. أن تقرأَ القرآنَ is an interpreted masdar, أن plus a verb, not a plain masdar noun, and a valid مفعول له must be a clear masdar. Because that condition is missing, a لام is assumed instead, and that is exactly the لِ shown before أن in sentence B. Sentence A, تدرسُ فاطمةُ التجويدَ أن تقرأَ القرآنَ, leaves that لام out, so it is wrong.

mafool-lahu-fihi-e06b.answer: Sentence A, صفحَ زيدٌ عن السفيهِ حِلمًا, is correct. حِلمًا is a clear masdar, it happens at the same time as the pardoning, صفحَ, and it belongs to the same doer, زيدٌ, who did the pardoning, so it meets every condition for a plain مفعول له, which takes the accusative ending with no لام, matching حِلمًا. Sentence B, صفحَ زيدٌ عن السفيهِ لِحِلمٍ, adds a لِ before حِلمٍ making it مجرور, but a لام is only added when one of the conditions is missing, and here nothing is missing, so B is wrong.

mafool-lahu-fihi-e07b.answer: Sentence A is correct because ابتغاءً is a clear masdar. The rule for a valid مفعول له says it must be a clear masdar, happen at the same time as the verb, and be related to the فاعل and nothing else. ابتغاءً meets all three: it is a plain masdar noun, it happens together with صامَ, and it belongs only to the same فاعل, زيدٌ, who fasted. Sentence B uses مبتغيًا instead, which is a noun describing the person wanting something, not a masdar at all, so it fails the clear masdar part of the rule and cannot be a مفعول له.

mafool-lahu-fihi-e08b.answer: Sentence B is correct because خوفاً is a clear masdar, it happens at the same time as the verb ابتعدتُ, and it belongs only to the same فاعل, the speaker, who moved away, so it meets every condition for a valid مفعول له. The rule says a مفعول له that meets its conditions takes منصوب, which matches خوفاً, since it has no لام. Sentence A adds لِ before خوف, giving لخوفٍ, مجرور, but the rule for adding a لام says a لام is only assumed when one of the conditions is missing, and here no condition is missing, so A is wrong.

mafool-lahu-fihi-e09b.answer: A is correct because أن يُأَدِّبَه fails the clear masdar condition for a valid مفعول له, since it is a sentence starting with أن, not a plain masdar noun. Because this condition is missing, the rule for adding a لام says a لام is then assumed, giving (لِ) أن يُأَدِّبَه. That is why A, which has the (لِ), is correct, and B, which drops it, is wrong.

mafool-lahu-fihi-e10b.answer: B is correct because ضعفَه fails one of the conditions for a valid مفعول له, that it must be related to the فاعل and nothing else: the weakness, ضعف, belongs to المكان, the place, not to أنت, the one entering, who is the فاعل of تدخل. Because this condition is missing, the rule for adding a لام says a لام is then assumed, giving لِضعفِه. A is wrong because it uses ضعفَه as a plain مفعول له even though its owner does not match the فاعل alone.

mafool-lahu-fihi-e11a.question: Look at the underlined words in أعطيتُ الفقيرَ خبزاً مَنْحَةً صباحًا شفقةً. For each of الفقير, خبزا, منحة, صباحا and شفقة, which Maf'ool (مفعول مطلق, مفعول به, مفعول معه, مفعول له or مفعول فيه) is it?

mafool-lahu-fihi-e11b.answer: الفقيرَ and خبزاً are both مفعول به, because they are the two things the giving act affects: the man given to, and the bread given. مَنْحةً is a مفعول مطلق, because it restates the giving itself as a gift, in the same sense as the verb أعطيتُ. صباحًا is a مفعول فيه, because it names the time the giving happened in, the morning. شفقةً is a مفعول له, because the rule says the مفعول له gives the reason for the action, and here it gives the reason he gave the bread, out of pity.

mafool-lahu-fihi-e11c.answer: I gave the poor man bread as a gift in the morning, out of pity.

mafool-lahu-fihi-e12a.question: Look at the underlined words in مَا بِكَ وزيدًا أمسِ فوقَ المسجدِ. For each of زيدا, أمس and فوق, which Maf'ool (مفعول مطلق, مفعول به, مفعول معه, مفعول له or مفعول فيه) is it?

mafool-lahu-fihi-e12b.answer: زيدًا is a مفعول معه. The و right before it does not mean plain and, it means along with: زيدًا is going along with the person being addressed at the same time, not simply added on as a separate thing. أمسِ is a مفعول فيه because it names when the state happened, yesterday. فوقَ is also a مفعول فيه, since the rule says the مفعول فيه signifies the time or the place an action is conducted in, and فوقَ gives the place, above the mosque.

mafool-lahu-fihi-e12c.answer: What is wrong with you, along with Zayd, yesterday, above the mosque?

mafool-lahu-fihi-e13a.answer: For each underlined word in the sentence (احترامًا, وكِتابَكَ, أمامَ, نَشاطًا), which مفعول is it: مفعول مطلق, مفعول به, مفعول معه, مفعول له, or مفعول فيه? (No change, this note passes.)
mafool-lahu-fihi-e13a.question: Look at the underlined words in احترامًا قُمتَ وكِتابَكَ أمامَ الأستاذِ نَشاطًا. For each of احتراما, كتابك, أمام and نشاطا, which Maf'ool (مفعول مطلق, مفعول به, مفعول معه, مفعول له or مفعول فيه) is it?

mafool-lahu-fihi-e13b.answer: احترامًا is a مفعول له, because it gives the reason you stood up. The rule for the مفعول له says it names the reason for an action, and the rule about its conditions says it must be a clear masdar that happens at the same time as the action and belongs only to the فاعل, which احترامًا satisfies. وكِتابَكَ is a مفعول معه, since the واو before it shows your book was with you while you stood, not a second thing doing the standing with you. أمامَ is a مفعول فيه, a ظرف مكان naming the place of the standing, matching the rule that the مفعول فيه names the time or the place of an action. نَشاطًا is a مفعول مطلق, an implied masdar describing the manner of the standing, energetically, not its reason, so it cannot be a مفعول له.

mafool-lahu-fihi-e13c.answer: Out of respect, you stood up with your book, in front of the teacher, energetically.

mafool-lahu-fihi-e14a.answer: For each underlined word in the sentence (الأصنامَ, فأسًا, يومَ, كَرْهًا), which مفعول is it: مفعول مطلق, مفعول به, مفعول معه, مفعول له, or مفعول فيه? (No change, this note passes.)
mafool-lahu-fihi-e14a.question: Look at the underlined words in إبراهيمُ كسرَ الأصنامَ فأسًا يومَ عيدِهم كَرْهًا للشرك. For each of الأصنام, فأسا, يوم and كرها, which Maf'ool (مفعول مطلق, مفعول به, مفعول معه, مفعول له or مفعول فيه) is it?

mafool-lahu-fihi-e14b.answer: الأصنامَ is the مفعول به, the thing Ibrahim broke. فأسًا, the axe, stands in for the missing masdar of the verb, so it is read as a مفعول مطلق, showing how the breaking was done, an implied 'a breaking with an axe'. يومَ is a مفعول فيه, a ظرف زمان naming the time of the action. كَرْهًا is a مفعول له, since it gives the reason, hatred of شرك: it is a clear masdar tied only to Ibrahim, the فاعل, and it happens at the same time as the breaking.

mafool-lahu-fihi-e14c.answer: Ibrahim broke the idols with an axe, on the day of their festival, out of hatred for shirk.

mafool-lahu-fihi-e15a.answer: For each underlined word in the sentence (اللَّه, تشريفًا, وَدينَه, كلَّ, أبدًا), which مفعول is it: مفعول مطلق, مفعول به, مفعول معه, مفعول له, or مفعول فيه? (No change, this note passes.)
mafool-lahu-fihi-e15a.question: Look at the underlined words in أَطِعِ اللَّه تشريفًا له وَدينَه كلَّ الإطاعةِ أبَدًا. For each of الله, تشريفا, دينه, كل and أبدا, which Maf'ool (مفعول مطلق, مفعول به, مفعول معه, مفعول له or مفعول فيه) is it?

mafool-lahu-fihi-e15b.answer: اللَّه is the مفعول به, the one being obeyed. تشريفًا is a مفعول له: it gives the reason for obeying, and it is a clear masdar tied to the فاعل, happening at the same time as the obeying. وَدينَه is marked as both مفعول به and مفعول معه, because the واو before it can be read two ways: it can join a second thing that is obeyed, His religion, or it can mean you obey Allah together with His religion at the same time, and both readings are possible here. كلَّ is a مفعول مطلق, a masdar type word (كلَّ الإطاعةِ, 'the whole of the obedience') describing the extent of the obeying, and أبَدًا is a مفعول فيه, an unrestricted time word meaning forever, naming the time of the action.

mafool-lahu-fihi-e15c.answer: Obey Allah in honour of Him, and His religion (or: together with His religion), with complete obedience, forever.

mafool-lahu-fihi-e16a.answer: For each underlined word in the sentence (مكَّةَ, ارتِجاءً, مغفرةَ), which مفعول is it: مفعول مطلق, مفعول به, مفعول معه, مفعول له, or مفعول فيه? (No change, this note passes.)
mafool-lahu-fihi-e16a.question: Look at the underlined words in دخلتُ مكَّةَ للعمرة ارتجاءً مغفرةَ اللهِ. For each of مكة, ارتجاء and مغفرة, which Maf'ool (مفعول مطلق, مفعول به, مفعول معه, مفعول له or مفعول فيه) is it?

mafool-lahu-fihi-e16b.answer: مكَّةَ is the مفعول به, the place entered, treated here as the direct object of دخلتُ. ارتجاءً is a مفعول له: it gives the reason for entering, and it is a clear masdar tied to the فاعل, happening at the same time as the entering. مغفرةَ is also a مفعول به, but of the hidden verb inside the masdar ارتجاءً itself; it is the thing being hoped for, Allah's forgiveness, joined to اللهِ as a مضاف إليه.

mafool-lahu-fihi-e16c.answer: I entered Makkah for Umrah, hoping for Allah's forgiveness.

mafool-lahu-fihi-e17a.question: For each underlined word, والأميرَ, القَهْقَرى and مساءً, which type of مفعول is it: مفعول مطلق, مفعول به, مفعول معه, مفعول له or مفعول فيه?

mafool-lahu-fihi-e17b.answer: الأميرَ is مفعول معه. The واو before it is a واو معية, a joining واو meaning 'along with', showing the army returned along with the commander at the same time, not a plain link joining two separate subjects. القَهْقَرى is مفعول مطلق: it is the masdar, the verbal noun meaning retreating backward, that restates and describes the manner of the verb رجعَ. مساءً is مفعول فيه, since it names the time the action happened in, the evening, matching the rule that the مفعول فيه signifies the time or the place of an action.

mafool-lahu-fihi-e17c.answer: The army returned, along with the commander, retreating backward, in the evening.

mafool-lahu-fihi-e18a.question: For each underlined word, السفينةَ, ليلًا and هُدُوءً, which type of مفعول is it: مفعول مطلق, مفعول به, مفعول معه, مفعول له or مفعول فيه?

mafool-lahu-fihi-e18c.answer: Zaid sailed the ship at night calmly, or, on the other reading the teacher allows, so that he himself would be at ease. Both readings of هُدُوءً are valid: a reason for sailing, or the manner of the sailing.

mafool-lahu-fihi-e01b.answer: Sentence B is correct: قرأتَ القرآنَ لِدُخولِكَ الجنَّةَ. دُخولَكَ is a clear masdar and it belongs only to the same doer as قرأتَ, you, so two of the conditions for a plain مفعول له are met. But entering Jannah does not happen at the same time as reading, it comes later, so the condition that the مفعول له must happen at the same time as the action is missing. When a condition is missing, a لام is assumed, which is exactly the لِ before دُخولِكَ in sentence B. Sentence A, قرأتَ القرآنَ دُخولَكَ الجنَّةَ, drops that لِ, so it is wrong. Translation: You read the Qur'an so that you enter Jannah.

mafool-lahu-fihi-e02b.answer: Sentence B is correct: أذهبُ إلى زيدٍ لطلبِه إيّايَ. طلبَه is a clear masdar, but the one doing the seeking is he, زيد, while the one going, the فاعل of أذهبُ, is I. Since a مفعول له must belong only to the same doer as the main verb, and here it belongs to a different person, that condition is missing. When a condition is missing, a لام is assumed, giving the لِ before طلبِه in sentence B. Sentence A, أذهبُ إلى زيدٍ طلبَه إيّايَ, drops that لِ, so it is wrong. Translation: I am going to Zaid because he is seeking me.

mafool-lahu-fihi-e03b.answer: Sentence A is correct: خشيةَ اللهِ صلُّوا صلواتِكُم. خشيةَ is a clear masdar, it happens at the same time as the praying, and it belongs to the same doer, you, who prays. Every condition for a plain مفعول له is met, so no لام is needed and خشيةَ simply takes the accusative ending on its own. Sentence B, بِخشيةِ اللهِ صلُّوا صلواتِكُم, adds a باء instead, but a missing condition is only ever replaced by a لام, never a باء, so B is wrong. Translation: Only because of fearing Allah, pray your prayers.

mafool-lahu-fihi-e04b.answer: Sentence A is correct: لِلإِلتقاءِ غدًا تكلَّمتُ بزيدٍ. The meeting is a clear masdar, but it is described as غدًا, tomorrow, while تكلَّمتُ, the speaking, already happened. Since a مفعول له must happen at the same time as the action it explains, and here the meeting is in the future while the speaking is in the past, that condition is missing. When a condition is missing, a لام is assumed, matching the لِ that opens sentence A. Sentence B, الالتقاءَ غدًا تكلَّمتُ بزيدٍ, drops that لِ, so it is wrong. Translation: Because of the meeting tomorrow, I spoke to Zaid.
